title: Day 709 — Sheinbaum Rebuffs Rubio's 'Ungoverned Territories' Cartel Claim, Calls It US Midterm Campaign Rhetoric
detail: On September 10, 2026 (Day 709, Thursday), at her National Palace mañanera, President Sheinbaum responded to remarks U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio made the previous day in Quito, Ecuador, where he said Mexico's fight against drug cartels is "not by far enough," that "there are vast territories in Mexico that are not governed by the State," and that the U.S. would confront the cartel threat "one way or another" if Mexico did not act in partnership with Washington. Sheinbaum said she believed the comments were timed to the United States' own November 2026 elections — "Creo que es parte de la campaña electoral de Estados Unidos. Ellos tienen elecciones en noviembre" — and repeated that "no se debe usar a México" as part of that campaign. She did not directly dispute Rubio's territorial-control claim but pointed to her government's security figures (a 53% drop in the national daily homicide average since October 2024, reported September 8, and fentanyl seizures down more than 70%) as evidence of sustained bilateral cooperation, including the joint "Águila Alta" anti-drone operation launched September 7 in the Tijuana-San Diego corridor. Separately, as Mexico's 2026–27 electoral process formally opened, Sheinbaum urged parties and aspirants ahead of the June 6, 2027 elections to "cumplan la ley, que no haya denostaciones, que haya propuestas," calling on media to guard against disinformation.

title: Day 709 — Economy Secretary Details Digital Economy Law, Sheinbaum Announces Zero VAT Rate for Books
detail: Also at the September 10, 2026 mañanera, the Secretariat of Economy detailed the Digital Economy Law for Digital and Electronic Payments — sent to the Chamber of Deputies alongside the 2027 Economic Package — which sets phased targets and timelines to shift public institutions, private companies and priority sectors from cash toward digital and electronic payment methods, with incentives and training tools aimed at helping micro and small businesses adopt secure electronic collection without hurting their income. Officials said more than 4.1 million taxpayers would benefit from simplified, fully digital tax procedures, including small businesses newly able to pay income tax on a quarterly rather than monthly basis. Separately, Sheinbaum announced books will be subject to a zero VAT rate rather than the standard exemption, allowing bookstores and publishers to recover VAT paid on their own expenses without the retail price to readers increasing.

media.caption: Economy Secretary details the Digital Economy Law and zero VAT rate for books at the September 10 mañanera
